A1.justification: Both PDFs describe PhyloLM. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support reliable comparison despite substantial expansion and reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original hyperparameter experiments, similarity matrices, phylogenetic reconstructions, and MMLU/ARC performance predictions, including code-context replications in Appendix D.

after.justification: v2 reports original phylogenetic analyses, predictions across six benchmarks, within-family analyses, and quantization experiments. These analyses qualify independently of the externally sourced benchmark scores.

M1.justification: Section 2.6 replaces 15-dimensional MDS of distances and a 200-hidden-unit MLP with 15-dimensional ICA of similarities and sigmoid logistic regression. This substantially changes the performance-prediction component. The underlying Nei similarity, distance transformation, and four-character sampling procedure remain.

E1.justification: Reported benchmark coverage expands from MMLU and ARC to include HellaSwag, TruthfulQA, WinoGrande, and GSM8K. The analyzed model population also adds Gemma and proprietary Claude, PaLM/Gemini, and Mistral models. Open-Web-Math and MBXP remain the context sources.

E2.justification: Neither version evaluates competing genealogy-inference or benchmark-prediction methods against PhyloLM. The added LLMs are study subjects, while GPTQ and AWQ in Appendix H concern quantized model inputs rather than alternative PhyloLM baselines.

E3.justification: Prediction changes from leave-one-model-out to leave-one-family-out evaluation. v2 also separates completion and chat interfaces and expands model configurations. Section 2.6 states that prediction excludes proprietary models, but Tables 4–5 include GPT results, leaving the precise inclusion protocol inconsistent.

E4.justification: v2 adds within-family correlations addressing whether prediction merely identifies model families, analyses of chat/completion interface effects in Appendix G, and quantization sensitivity across Qwen1.5 model sizes in Appendix H. The existing gene-count/probe-count sensitivity studies and math/code comparisons are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions use eight independently sampled gene sets and show hyperparameter error bars; v2 newly identifies those bars as SEM. It additionally reports correlation summaries with SEM and confidence-interval displays, Student's t-tests, family-specific p-values and sample counts, and a quantization significance test. No increase in repeated runs is established.

E6.justification: The two-benchmark prediction plots are replaced by substantially expanded results under the revised predictor and family-held-out protocol. Tables 4–5 newly report overall MMLU correlations of 0.88 for math contexts and 0.79 for code contexts. Appendix H adds quantization rankings and model-size trends. These are new results under changed conditions, not demonstrated same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: The Nei similarity formula, negative-log distance transformation, population/context/token analogy, and variability computations are retained. Explicit averaging notation and Appendix C pseudocode clarify existing computations without introducing substantive mathematical results, formal assumptions, or proofs.

C1.justification: The central claims remain output-based reconstruction of model relationships and inexpensive benchmark prediction. The Discussion adds a claim that PhyloLM reveals how quantization fidelity depends on model size, modestly broadening its stated utility.

C2.justification: v2 identifies chat-interface prompting as a confound in interpreting model distances, substantially qualifying v1's interpretation of isolated proprietary-model branches. It also argues against family-only prediction using new controls, acknowledges the code reconstruction's incorrect root, expands family-specific interpretations, and adds the limitation that temperature effects were not investigated.

D1.justification: Appendices A–C substantially expand reproducibility information: dataset fields and sizes, sampling temperature 0.7 and top-p 1, A100 memory and GPU allocation, the Falcon180B precision exception, API access details, benchmark-score sources and prompting settings, and algorithm pseudocode. These are principally newly documented details, not evidence that retained experiments were rerun.

R1.justification: v2 adds references supporting the expanded study, including PaLM, Gemini, Gemma, Mixtral, GPTQ, AWQ, MergeKit, the Open LLM Leaderboard, and GPT-Fathom. The central positioning as an adaptation of population-genetic methods remains unchanged.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, methods explanations, results narrative, and discussion are extensively rewritten. Headings and terminology are revised, including replacing much of 'genome' with 'set of genes'. Limitations are integrated into the Discussion, and the appendix is reorganized into dedicated algorithm, interpretation, prediction, and quantization sections.

P2.justification: The main text changes from two columns to one. The analogy and reconstruction diagrams are redrawn, global rooted dendrograms become separate unrooted completion/chat displays, and model tables gain benchmark columns. New statistical panels and quantization figures substantially change the visual presentation; named dendrograms are supplied separately in Appendix I.

improvement.justification: v1 explicitly leaves unresolved whether predictions merely reflect model families. v2 directly addresses this weakness through family-held-out evaluation and within-family analyses, while recognizing interface confounds and substantially improving experimental documentation. These changes strengthen the paper beyond simply adding benchmarks. Inconsistent GPT inclusion, retained MLP/point-held-out caption wording, and discrepancies between statistical summaries and appendix tables weaken auditability, but the overall methodological and reproducibility gains remain substantial.
